title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 8 Media Availability | Monday, October 26th | Press Conference
text: Very well, we obviously watched the recording and there were some really great performances.  I think the guys were very physical in that game and the statistic was plus four in turnover margin.  I think it's like a 92% win rate there.  That really set us up for success in that game because of how we attacked the ball defensively, but there were great individual efforts, I'm proud of the guys in that regard, and now we need to quickly turn the page and move on to a divisional rival.  But having said that , I will accept any questions.    We'll go with Mark first. Which Mark are we talking about? Mark Lombardi, go ahead. Okay, thanks Zeno.  Coach, it's interesting, Mike Penix just completed his seventeenth career start due to injuries and all that, and I'm wondering, generally speaking, when you evaluate quarterbacks, what's that timeframe like and how would you evaluate Mike right now? Well, I think any player improves with more turns, that's obvious, regardless of the position you play.  So, for any quarterback, the more experience you have facing different defenses and being put in different situations, the better it can be .  And I think that's what I see in Mike: he's accumulating these games, both literally, the wins and all that, and accumulating all these experiences and learning from them.  And in the games, we've seen a lot of different coverages, a lot of different pressures, different philosophies, and in the red zone, all of that.  So I just think you should do your best to learn from each of these experiences and try to improve week by week as these seasons progress. Josh Kendall. Hi, Kevin.  Um, the mantra is always that we put our guys in, you know, we adapt our system to the strengths of our players.  With Mike, he's playing differently than he had before, at least before college.  What gave you the feeling that this offensive style was right for him? Well, Josh, I can't necessarily speak about the university and previous systems.  I mean, I've seen the recording.  You know, I think the obvious change that you guys have pointed out and asked questions about is playing low center versus shotgun versus pistol.  Yes, I mean, that's different, but there are also many similarities to things he's done in the past. Again, in universities and among professionals.  Well, I just think it's an evolution of the player.  As we discussed in the previous question, an evolution based on the repetitions we are obtaining.  So I think we're still trying to put Mike in the best possible position.  One way to start is by keeping your quarterback clean.  And I give a lot of credit to our guys yesterday for not allowing any captures.  I believe there was only one blow to the marshal.  That's the recipe for any marshal of any system and in any era to succeed: give him time and a clean purse to operate with. Mark Zenno. Kevin, after the game you said that you told the team that it was an identity game for you. Can you explain a little more what that means to you, what that identity is, and how they can maintain it going forward? Well, yes, I can.  Also, and I mentioned this, it's easy to talk about.  It's easy to have an identity for your offense, your defense, your special teams, and for your team.  And we have it.  And all teams have it.  But I think the important point for me, Mark, in explaining that or wanting to talk about it with our team, was to go back to who we are and what our style of play is.  And I felt we were a very physical football team yesterday.  That has to be our way of playing.  That's in our DNA.  That's what should define us, and I think they saw the open receivers blocking the deep ones.  They saw the offensive linemen displacing opponents from the ball.  Defensively they saw very good examples of tackling, double tackling alongside your teammate in the zone.  So , I guess another way to put it, Mark, would be: being who we are and that the game is, in the end, about us and playing according to what we have decided is our identity , more than anything else. Daniel Flick. Hi, Kevin.  How are you? Hello, Daniel. When Jesse was there, if I'm not mistaken, I think you had to play against him at least three years in a row in Cleveland, right? Do you remember the challenge he presented and how happy you were when he left? Yes, you know, I've always had the highest opinion of Jesse as a player.    I did n't know the person, so I feel very blessed and fortunate to know him now and see the incredible impact he has on our football team, of course on the field, but also throughout this entire building. You know, safeties who are attentive to the ball are a real challenge for an offense, because these guys have a way of finding the ball , they have a way in zone defense of reading the quarterbacks' eyes , and they have a way in man defense of literally playing the ball like Jessie did a couple of times.  I was, you know, thinking about that time I was covering Kittle towards the end of the game.  He's just very, very focused on the ball.  He is alert to the ball when the other team runs with it and hits it to take it away.  It's very deliberate.  So I think these deep-lying guys, these, you know, the so-called " ball chasers," of which I think Jessie is one.  The ball comes to him and it's not just because he's doing his job, being in the right place, but like the greats, he has the ability to go and get the ball when it's in the air.    I was chatting with Josh Woods yesterday about him and he brought up the point that he's like everyone's idol.  As if everyone wanted to watch how he operates and play behind him and support him. Intangibly, how unique is he in your eyes?  Jessie, I mean. Well, intangibles are difficult to express in words, I suppose.  I would just tell them that he's a veteran.  The boys trust him, his teammates trust him. Certainly, we as coaches , trust him.  And you need to have guys who lead by example. You need to have guys who lead by sometimes saying a lot.  Jessie finds that right balance simply by being himself.  Go ahead, Josh. Kevin, since Mike came back, you guys lead the league in scoring.  Does it feel that way for you? You know, I don't really obsess too much over statistics.  It's important to know them because I think it's important to know... I need to know what the opposition knows, so to speak.  But the annotations do n't really influence that.  You know, the turnover margin: I can tell you we're at minus three after seven weeks, and I can tell you we were second to last two weeks ago .  So we're moving in the right direction in that respect. But as for other statistics, I'm aware of them, but they don't really affect me, if you will. Mark Raimondi. Speaking of turnovers, coach, something Mike has demonstrated in his 17 starts is that he hardly ever loses the ball .  How important is that, and what does that trait develop, would you say? Taking care of the ball is a great virtue to have in the quarterback position .  Bernie Kosar had a great record for passes attempted without an interception for a long time, which I think was perhaps surpassed by Rodgers.  But those quarterbacks who don't let the other team touch them.  That's a big deal in this league.  Now, you're going to throw interceptions.  It's an occupational hazard.  It's going to happen.  But understanding when to take a risk and when to shoot hard at a closed window because the game requires it, and when to make a short pass , I think is a matter of instinct .  Of course, we train it with all our boys and we always teach it to them and point out how important it is.  What you don't want is a quarterback who always decides to play short and not advance the ball up the field, and that's definitely not Mike , nor is it how we train.  We want them to seize opportunities when they arise, and when they don't, we want them to make big decisions. Dillard. Go ahead, Mark Zenno.  We'll come back to you, Dillard. Dillard is still having problems with his microphone.  Dillard, send me your question by message, man.  Kev, you guys talk a lot about starting fast, right?  And to be able to execute better at the beginning of the game .  That wasn't necessarily the case, although you did recover, but how do you work to correct that and improve on getting off to a fast start? Well, again, you can talk about it all you want and we will.  There are certain things we've done over time, including recently, where you add a competitive period to the start of practice.    We did it .  You might get some messages, either on game day or during the week, to try and adjust some things in your biological clock, but in the end, like everything else, it's about executing at the start of the game.  And executing early in the game means that we as coaches have given the guys a plan that they understand and can play quickly.  And, well, it's not much more complicated than that. Darius. Hey Kevin, we saw the early reversal for Zachariah Branch at the beginning, as well as the kickoff return.  What does this tell the rest of the team when you see a guy have a week like the one he had last week and now, at the beginning of this one, be able to have a big impact? Yes, I thought Zachariah played really well in that game. Obviously, that great comeback got us going.  I think he did well in the other comebacks as the second in charge.  Um, you know, he's a guy who also made plays in the aerial game.  So, he's definitely someone we trust, someone quarterbacks trust.  Their role will only continue to grow. Eli, can you try again? Sorry about that.  Very good, thank you guys.  Thank you. Yes, thanks guys.

There was always there's always a path and sometimes the path is pretty narrow and it felt like that, you know, and and uh the wind was a factor and and it affected uh our passers like just like it affected Jordan Love. Just for us, it's this is the next game. This is the next championship opportunity. But I'm also fully aware there's a human element involved. And, uh, you know, for us, you know, coming off of that loss in the in the fashion that we lost, um, for the Packers, you know, a really tough loss for them as well. title: Michael Pierce Joins The Lounge | Baltimore Ravens
text: [music] Welcome into the lounge. I'm Ryan Mink here with Garrett Downing and we are thrilled to sit down with Michael Pierce who is going to be one of our new co-hosts on Ravens Daily 3 to 5 every weekday. It's going to be on WB posted as a podcast as well as on TV. So, Michael, thrilled to have you join the team, man. Going from player now to the dark side on the media. What's it like going from answering questions to now asking questions? >> I think it's cool, man. I think I have uh I think I have some good questions to ask that maybe, >> you know, you guys who haven't played ball as long can ask. [laughter] >> Hey, you on the they're on the safe side, right? So, uh no, I think I just have a unique perspective. I should be able to get some good answers from guys and uh like I said, I still see those guys as family. So, I think it should be a fun fun fun venture for me. >> Yeah, we're excited to have you join our team here and be part of this. And like Ryan said, this is a brand new radio show that's going to air locally here and beyond two hours a day, Monday through Friday, uh, as well as live streamed on our channels as well. And so for you, like what made this an opportunity that you wanted to pursue and to to jump jump into? >> Uh, I think first and foremost, I just always enjoy media. So, uh, I still talk on like Glenn Radio, uh, Glen Clark radio. Uh, they call me I just did someone else's radio show not too long ago. Um, I actually got involved with Blackwing Podcast with uh two of my guys uh I met at the Senior Bowl, Ravens fans. So, um, no, the media space is always interesting. Um, I know a lot of former athletes are getting in the media, right? But, uh, just to have it here, um, and not have to talk about everybody else cuz sometimes you just don't care about, you know, whatever team may be doing what, but I'll always care about what the Ravens have going on. So, uh, being able to help spotlight my guys, um, for organization I love, for city I love is one million for me. Well, look, I I always remember when we had you on the lounge in the early days in your career uh after you made the team as an undrafted rookie, and I enjoyed telling your story. So, let's just say that that planted the seed of the media interest in you that has now blossomed today to to have you being doing this full-time, which is really cool. >> Yeah. Yeah. No, man. Uh you and Cass are always awesome. Um that did that let me know that I have a uh a voice in some stuff that people want to hear. Um you don't always know that until, you know, you get a warm review or people say, "Oh, you did really well." Yeah. >> So, um, no, I I definitely appreciate you guys. >> How much have you been following the Ravens since your days here ended? >> Just as much as any other, you know, probably Ravens fanatical fan. Um, like I said, I play with a lot of these guys, so, uh, I'm obviously not a part of the team, but, um, I still feel like I'm a part of the team, if you will, but every game I don't miss. So, >> Right. Right. Right. and and just, you know, what do you expect kind of going from playing where obviously the the stakes are very high, high pressure and all those things to the emotions of now being on the media side where, you know, you're in front of a camera and in front of a mic, you know, what do you expect the difference to be there? >> Uh, I think it's just a switching of my brain, if you will. So, um, >> I [snorts] don't have to perform physically, but I have to perform mentally. I have to be sharp. I have to know what I'm talking about. I have to be a breast on the analytics and the stats and all that kind of stuff which I find interesting anyway. Um for me I was more of a uh technical player so I had to pay attention to finalities and all those different type of things. So um I think it's just switching my brain over um obviously watching the games and just being more analytical um being a breast on what may be going on what may be going on throughout the game and uh not only that but throughout the future how everybody thinks and all that kind of stuff. So uh no I think it's awesome man. >> Yeah. Well, I can't wait to see how many times we show your interception. The highlight of [laughter] your That's going to be brought up, I think, a few times. What do you think? >> Listen, people think that was the only play I made in [laughter] the pros. You made that one play and I was like, "Yeah, but I was a fairly decent player for like [laughter] eight years, right?" But, uh, no, man. I I have grown tired of seeing it, but it brings so much joy to people like you would never believe. So, uh, even people down in Alabama and all those random things, places that you may not think people would see Ravens football, they saw that play, whether it's on Facebook or Instagram, all that stuff. So, um, now that is what I've become famous for and I I just kind of I took it. I tell you what a great >> wild how viral that play went. Insane. >> It was nutty. >> Very insane. So, uh, like I said, what they say, the working clock is wrong, right? Twice a day. [laughter] That's right. >> That was my one time to be where I was supposed to be. I can't wait till like Travis Jones gets the interception and you get to break that down. >> It's going to be waiting for that. >> Insane cuz Travis going to run and it's going to be funny. [laughter] >> Well, yeah. I mean, you have the ultimate quote at the end of that one, which is the bus was out of gas, which is just hilarious, too, to add on top of that play. It's kind of like, you know, every band has a greatest hit, you know, like this is the song you close out the concert with every time. Like that play for you, like that's the greatest hit, which is like, you know, it's it's uh it's a good thing to have a play like that people remember. That's that's a sign of success. >> Yeah. No, man. Look, I I grew up watching and idolizing Vince Wilfork and all those guys. I I wasn't as great of a noseguard as those guys, right? But, uh, it somehow happened that I have a play that might outlive all of us. So, uh, no, that's something I take joy in, man. So, uh, no, it it was a good way to to end my career and have it be at home. Uh, and Mnt Bank was awesome, bro. You know, so we were just in the cafeteria and as we were sitting down there, felt like everybody came by and said hello and was excited to see you, players, coaches, and and it just as you mentioned, like you still have a lot of good relationships in this building, played with a lot of the guys who were still on this team. How much of that is something that you're excited to kind of be back in this environment here in this building every day? You're literally going to broadcast from right here where we do the lounge. Uh this is where you're going to do the radio show as well. So, uh, how excited are you to just be in this in this space, in this building every single day? >> Yeah, like I said a few, uh, moments earlier, man, I still feel like I'm a part of the team, even though I'm way back in Bama, right? So, uh, I still feel like I have a connection to when Rocoan does well and Travis holds up a block. So, um, no, just to be around the guys, be around some of the coaches that still here, you guys, Miss Val, Manny, everybody's still doing their thing. And I'm a world away in Alabama, man. It's it's it's a blessing, bro. Uh it's hard to explain and put into words like um just to see people's warm reaction to me coming back here, right? Um that's something you can't it's very genuine, right? You can't make that up. So uh no, I'm glad I left everyone with a uh a positive thought about myself and uh for everybody to hap to be happy to welcome me back is is super super special. >> When when you retired, did you think like, man, I would hope to get into the media space? Because sometimes guys, as you're playing, you're kind of like, hey, this is this is the next chapter for me. I want to go in this direction. At what point for you did this become something that you felt like, hey, I would really like to pursue that. [clears throat] >> Like I said, I always enjoyed the interviews. Um, I didn't know this job was coming open at all. Uh, I kind of joked with my wife and said, I wonder if I'll be good enough to get this spot. Um, but like I said, I've done some some work with uh Blackwing Podcast and a few other podcasts, but um to see myself having this job on the daily was not on my radar to be quite honest. Um, so I'm actually coaching uh a school down named Gulf Shores down in uh Alabama. So, um, no, man. Like I said, this uh this is a welcome welcome change of direction that is definitely wasn't in my plans, but uh I'm blessed to be able to have enough talent to secure the job and be able to learn for guys like Kyle and everyone. >> Did did you think that coaching was going to be kind of your postc career move or or what did you see when you first retired? >> Yeah, so um I that was my plan. and I knew I wanted to stay around the game, right? Um, so >> I took a job at my alma mater. Um, >> family reasons kind of made me make made me move back home. >> Um, so >> I [snorts] knew I always wanted to impact guys, help guys learn the game, grow the game, give them some game about going to college and all that kind of stuff. So, um, I think the high school game probably was the best spot for me at that time. So, um, yeah, took a job at G Shores. uh been helping guys kind of, you know, maneuver through high school, kind of figure out this NIL stuff and all that kind of stuff. So, um no, it's been good to coach guys, give back the knowledge that I've gained and uh just be around the game in some capacity, right? So, um >> yeah. No, like I said, it's uh it's been a super super interesting process, but um I I would be lying too if I told you I had this in mind. >> Yeah. How tough is it uh you know, to have the game to stop playing the game? And you know, you hear a lot of players, you they want to still be around it. >> You know, when when you're not playing anymore, can you explain how difficult that transition is and how much it does help to stay around it in some way? >> Yeah. Um, I think the thing that especially like fans don't always notice and they always gripe, but like athletes get like very uh sensitive when people critique their work. Um, I think and I think it helps me >> in this space, right? Help guys and people understand like this is our life's work. So, I've been playing football since four years old. Stopped at 32. Obviously, I learned a lot of things in college. I got a degree. Um, the things I could do on the corporate side, but um, like I said, for most part, this is what I wanted to do since I was four years old. >> So, um, when that ends, I can definitely see how people um, who don't have a plan or they their career like ends abruptly, especially like if you had like super highs or you know what I mean? Um, those things end. It's kind of like what do you do now? um I don't think you can like recreate the camaraderie and the environment that um football creates not only even in professional but high school and even college right so I think this this is a very special sport and it kind of allows guys to grow you get men challenging men to be better men being better on and off the field so um it's not too much like it quite honestly so uh no for me I think that's always this is always be a space I'll be in >> one thing I thought think is cool about your story is you've had a couple different homecomings here to Baltimore. You started your career here. Then you went and you played for the Vikings for a couple years. Then you came back. So that was the first homecoming. Then you retired and now and then you went back home to Alabama. Now you're coming back here to Baltimore. What is it about this area, this region, this team that kind of keeps pulling you back? >> Well, I mean, so you think about it like this. Most of my adult formative years and memories and all that stuff, court memories are like really literally here. uh you spend the offseason maybe two or three months out of the year uh you know wherever you may be Alabama or wherever athletes choose to live but for the most part I grew up and became an adult and learned who I am as a person and for the most part in this community so um I have a local church um looking for a CrossFit gym but like I said I know people um for us especially myself like I have family that actually lives here they've been here way before I was born so um no it just feels like coming home man and like I said I've I've resurrected a name for myself here. Long way from Alabama, obviously that's something I could never dream of and a million a million million dreams. So, um no, this place is a special place in my heart. Um I'm glad to be able to find a job doing something I love. Um and in a community that I love. So, um like I said, I've always done community service and those kind of things up here and uh I was doing my best to try to do that as well when I was still down in Bama. So, uh, to be able to be able to be here and, uh, impact guys and impact the community is something that, um, >> is unique. And, uh, shout out to J Mlan. >> Okay. >> He was one of the first ones to come back and work here. >> Yeah. >> Oh, you saying you saw you saw J come back [clears throat] and work here in your college. That could be >> that could be a dope the dope path. Yeah. >> Now you're doing it yourself. >> Yep. Yep. Yep. So, uh, God works in mysterious ways, man. >> Yeah. tell tell viewers and listeners what they can expect from Ravens Daily. What kind of conversations do you want to have on there? >> Obviously, we'll bring players along, >> but um it's just going to be uh you know, Kyle Yman's one nemy. Um he's a very accomplished guy. Me also learning and seeing things from a different perspective. Obviously, I'll give like a players for view as well as just an informed football point of view on different things. But, um I think it's just going to be a really really good informed conversation. Like I said, you'll have your analytics, but you'll also have your opinion based things and uh some things that I want to defend for players and vice versa, >> obviously with Kyle being from the media space. So, um I think it'll be a good uh a good mix of personalities, a good mix of viewpoints, and uh I think I think fans will enjoy it. >> Now, now as a former defensive lineman, are you going to be more gentle on defensive lineman or does that make you more critical? [laughter] >> What do you think? >> I think it'll be a good mix of both, quite honestly. Um, like I said, obviously I've played with Kas. I play with Beaks. I play with Trady. The list can go on, right? Um, but at at some point, like I am still a media member. I have to do my job. And if we happen not to have a good game, it's okay to say that. And, um, I think those guys know my personality well enough to know that I'm not attacking them personally, obviously. Right. >> We just won't do that, >> right? >> We just have great games all the time. >> We just won't do great, right? [laughter] >> right? So, uh, no, man. Um, I think I think it'll be a good mix of both, but at the same time, like I said, I think everybody knows my personality and know who I am. And uh, no, we're going to tell the truth for sure. >> I'm curious, when you're watching a game, are you just watching it like casually watching the ball just like everybody else, or do you kind of zone in, zero in on the defensive line play? Like, how do you just watch it as a viewer and your perspective during a game? >> Um, so anybody who's been to my house during Ravens games, they hate it. Um, and I normally [clears throat] just watch I have like a TV and then I have my computer. So like I'll like rewind a lot of stuff. So like we end up behind the live broadcast quite a bit. >> Like this game takes six hours. >> I'm trying to figure out why stuff is happening, right? So like especially when um we were running the same plays when I retired, I could kind of see what formations we're in, how we're lined up, and kind of figure out what play we're running, right? And then why stuff isn't working. Um it wasn't to do talk on the media, but it was just for my own brain, right? So that's kind of how we've been wired to think, right? So, um, no, it's not fun for regular fans who just want to watch the game, but for me, like I also like to see what's wrong, but I if we watch like a pack like Packers and uh Cowboys yesterday, [snorts] >> I didn't uh I didn't rewind it once. >> It's just for us, right? Yeah. Just to see what guys are doing and how things are playing out. So, um yeah, it it's probably not fun, but it's very analytical. >> Yeah. Well, that perspective is good. It's valuable and that's uh and that's what you're going to bring to Ravens Daily. And uh we're excited to have you on the show and uh again, Michael's going to be hosting it along with Kyle Yman's uh 3 to 5 Monday through Friday. Uh going to be able to listen to it on WBL radio. Uh it's going to be a podcast after the fact each day. Also going to live stream on the Ravens app and website YouTube channel. So there's going to be a lot of different ways uh to watch it and consume it. And I really look forward to the conversation that you guys are going to have on there each day. >> Awesome, brother. Thank you'all for having me. >> Thank you, Mike. >> Awesome. Thank you, Mike.

title: '26 Season So Far, Trade Deadline, Post-Bye Week Jags | Jaguars Happy Hour
text: [bell] >> It is Monday, October 26th. This is Jaguars Happy Hour. Jaguars Happy Hour is brought to you by Jet Home Loans. And now, a gal who can do anything she wants because she's Banaszak strong. Kainani Stevens. >> And honor I appreciate that. Welcome to Jaguars Happy Hour, Kainani Stevens. Here with the Austin Lane and Pete Prisco. Pete Banaszak passing away of Raiders Holy Roller fame, but also was with the Jags as well, right Pete? >> Yeah, yeah. He was he was around town for a long time. Pete was Pete was a one-of-a-kind man. He was he was a tough old man. He was tough as could be. And anybody remembers him when he played, he was a tough football player, too. Yeah, Pete was a good man. >> Um I was enjoying I I went back and watched one of the NFL films about the Holy Roller incident and they were just talking about how the entire Raiders team was out karaokeing in San Diego until like 4:00 in the morning. So, that's why they were playing like crap at that point. And then they were just trying to salvage something at the end of the game. So, I always enjoy those old stories. >> That was a wild bunch now. >> I I don't doubt it. I don't doubt it. Just look at it. >> didn't have social media back then where everybody found out what you were doing, either. >> [laughter] >> You could actually have some fun. Sounds like a good time. Well, we had some fun. We had a bye week. Pete doesn't get a bye week. Pete's always working, but we we had a bye week. We had a Jaguars bye week. So, hopefully everybody got to do whatever they needed to do. Clean out the garage, get your chores done, get some brunch in because now we're back to football. We are going to talk today. We've got some stuff coming up for you featuring, you know, what went on in the bye week, obviously. It's a bye week win for me, I'm saying, because you didn't play, but some other people won and that helped you out in the long term. Also, buyers or sellers. we're 2 weeks out now from the trade deadline, so we've been talking about that every single week, and we're going to continue to do that here as well. We're going to keep it real, and we are going to answer fan questions that have come in. If you have any more, send them to me on Twitter. I'll ask them on the show, because why not? So, Pete, you keep track of everybody, and and I I watched a little bit of football, not a ton this weekend, but it's always good when if you're not playing, at least everybody else in the division is also losing. That has to help. >> I mean, after what happened last week in London, everybody started again with "Oh, the Texans are back. They're going to take the division." And then they got home, and the Giants really put it to them. I mean, you know, I know it was close at the end, but they were dominating that game. They They controlled the whole flow of that game. And the Scat back run, if he doesn't pull up with the hamstring, he probably scores. And then they score on the next play. I mean, they pushed them around. They were more physical. And I think the fact that they lost, the Colts look awful and lost, and the Titans continue to look bad. I Dare I say that the division's over? I mean, I I I don't want to quite go that far, but man, I tell you what, it sure has a feel of that. >> You know, Pete, it really does. And listen, I was drinking that Kool-Aid thinking, okay, Houston Texans beat Jacksonville in London. C.J. Stroud kind of looks like a top, you know, we'll call him a top seven quarterback in the league, like and they have an easy schedule, so we thought with the Giants coming up, I thought for sure the Texans would be right back in it. And give the Giants a lot of, you know, credit here, because I had the Texans winning this game by a by a bunch, um simply because new quarterback, De'Von Achane and everything, but I was really impressed with the New York Giants defense. And this is a defense, maybe much like in Jacksonville, hasn't got to the quarterback a lot, right? Despite some pretty big names in that defense, but to me, Pete, and and this is where I I kind of bring it to a Jay Glazer's point a little bit, if you look at what the Giants did to that Texans offense. Now, and I get that the box score says one thing, Stroud had a pretty, you know, he had two touchdowns and everything. Stroud wasn't himself. Nico Collins was was definitely held in check. And it's all because to me as De'ante Banks essentially said, "I'm going to cover Nico Collins one-on-one, press him, man coverage." And we saw what the benefits were of that. So I I I saw Banks do his thing. I'm like, "Man, could Travis Hunter essentially do the exact same thing in this Jaguars defense and maybe give him a little more, you know, oomph, if you will?" >> Yeah, that's how I would play it. I wouldn't have blitzed him as much as the Jaguars did the last time they played him, but but I think that the fact that De'ante Banks is not as good a corner as Travis Hunter and and he was able to limit him and and look, we know what Collins is. He's a physical, tough receiver, but he's not going to really run by you consistently. He's not that guy. So I think Travis Hunter could do that the next time. But who knows? By the time they play that next game, it might not really matter more that much. Who, you know, but but you know what? The Texans schedule softens here a little bit. If you look at the next 3 weeks, I I think we would sit here and say that, but they didn't beat the Giants at home. In fact, they've lost four home games already. That's amazing when you think about it. >> I'm just shocked that obviously you're going to get up for a divisional game against the Jaguars. I think both teams enjoy playing each other at this point cuz they want to win. But then immediately having a letdown as soon as you get home, like you think, you know, you want to get back to Houston, get your first win, wearing your terrible battle red uniforms, like you need to get something. And there was just no It felt like they went completely reverted right back. >> And and it's one thing to be bad on offense, but their defense, you know, lacked the physicality in the middle. That their defense gave up some big plays to Malik Neighbors and then especially uh, you know, A.J. McCarthy, who we haven't talked about it seems like in a year, comes out and has an efficient day. And at the end of the day, like, yeah, their offense can be up and down. Their defense has to be playing on all cylinders. You you you have a defensive-minded coach in DeMeco Ryans, who's responsible for for that defense and they didn't show up. So like if if if if if I'm Texans fans, if I'm that locker room, if I'm management, I'm like, Demeco, what are we doing right now? >> Well, remember he took over play-calling duties the week they beat the Titans. Really tough duty for you, Demeco. Then he played at Jacksonville, the Jaguars moved the football on them any all day. And now you have the [clears throat] Giants moving the football on them all day. And you know, before the season everybody talked about how great that defense would be. That's going to be one of the most disappointing units in all of the National Football League. I mean, they just aren't very good right now. >> P, is it just are they aging a little bit? Is it different cuz they're not a ton of different personnel? >> No, it's not age. It's because they're still young. But like Stingley hasn't played as well as he's played. Laster has been bad. The safeties haven't been as good. You know, they've had injuries at linebacker and that's impacted the defense. And then you go to the you know, you want to run on them. That's what you want to do. If you run on them, it kind of neutralizes the pass rush a little bit. Will Anderson didn't have a sack on Sunday. It means it's two straight games where he hasn't had a sack. And that usually doesn't happen. So, yeah, I I think the more physical you are with them, you bully the bully. That's the old adage. Bully the bully. And I think that's what the Giants did to them. >> Well, they probably got to get-right game cuz they got the Chargers coming up. Uh I think they have a bye week and then they have the Chargers coming up. So. >> Well, but you think about it, the Chargers are 0 and 6. That And that's at LA. That's not an easy game for them. Even even as bad as the Chargers have been, they're going to get some guys back healthy. And then then they have two games after that that are relatively winnable if I'm not mistaken, right? >> Well, they have Browns who are apparently good now. And then >> [clears throat] >> and then the Colts, which what the Colts will be at that point on November 19th, I'm not sure. >> Well, and keep in mind who the Chargers are, too. I mean, they have a pretty proud coach, I feel like in Jim Harbaugh, that like the head of quarterback that is going to lay down and and die for the Houston Texans. Especially a Houston Texans team that's won only two games this season, right? So, um I feel like they probably got to win that game as well how they're feeling in that locker room, too. >> Absolutely. >> P, let's talk a little bit about the Colts as well because obviously they fired their GM. We were assuming they're they're now fully tail spinning. Is this the fire sale this week, next week? Like have they posted the dates of the sale yet? When is this happening? >> Well, they haven't posted it yet, but those I think there's a lot of people who are going to be available. I really do. And and and for the price, you're not just going to give them away. What's it going to take to get Jonathan Taylor? I mean that's a that's a legitimate question. What's it going to take to get Quenton Nelson? What's it going to take to get DeForest Buckner? Those are the kind of the guys you're looking at and you know, somebody said a first round pick for Jonathan Taylor. I wouldn't do that. He's got a lot of wear and tear on that body. And a lot of wear and tear at Wisconsin. >> Mhm. >> But maybe a two, a you know, and something else down the line you'll get get him. If I were the Jaguars, I would call on Buckner. >> I don't think the Colts would trade him into division, but you never know. They're desperate. They need draft picks. Uh so I would call on Buckner. And then and then the other one is uh you know, when you look at the the guard, Quenton Nelson, you know, there's also some value there if they wanted to trade him. So this team needs draft picks and and that's why I think they're they're going to be really active sellers as we get closer to the trade deadline. >> DeForest Buckner's is his contract up the end of the year? I feel like >> Yes. Yes. So it'll be a rental. So so basically if you're the Colts, you say, "Hey, we don't know if he'd go back to Jacksonville cuz he probably wouldn't. So do we care cuz we're not competing anyway. So do we care if they take him?" So that that's kind of what the >> That would be. >> Might be more on their side. Plus reunite him with his buddy Arik Armstead in the middle there, Pete. >> Yeah, then Arik Armstead doesn't need to play 45 plays a game game cuz he shouldn't be playing 45 plays a game. >> They can split it. >> Pete, I mean how realistic cuz like I'm with you. I think the Colts, you know, firing their GM, they're definitely in sell mode. But if you look at they're two and five right now, one and one in the division, right? So right now what? They're two I guess it'd be two and a half games back, right? Cuz the Jaguars have the bye. But they played Jacksonville twice. But I agree with you. It feels like they're in sell mode. Should they be though? I guess is the the I mean when when do you actually go to sellmo because they can theoretically they can still win some games and >> Well, you have a couple weeks. You what you got what to November 10th. So, you got you got a little bit of time. So, if they lose, let's just say they never win in Jacksonville. So, that's I mean, come on. >> just leave him there after the game. >> What? >> Just tell him he's got to be like, "Okay, we're it's official. You can just stay." >> I mean, they haven't won there since what? 2014, right? It's the last time they won there. >> lock possibility. >> Andrew Luck was their quarterback. >> It's been a minute. >> Yeah, so so if let's just say Jacksonville wins that game, then any hope of winning the division is gone for them. And if it's gone by the trade deadline, then you absolutely have to ask to make moves. And and I don't think Look, they're not a very good football team right now. Daniel Jones doesn't look right after the Achilles. He just hasn't been the same player. And they had they don't have Pierce. You know, they just don't scare you down the field. >> Sauce has been hurt. >> line is still pretty solid. >> Yeah. >> Defensive line can be when when, you know, Stewart hasn't been as good, but Buckner is still good. But I just don't think it's a good football team and I think they kind of see the handwriting on the wall. When you start talking about trading off assets, that's tough to deal with in the locker room. >> Yeah, you already heard them talking out. I feel like players were already kind of getting disgruntled a couple weeks ago. And at this point, if you're in a locker room like that, it's it's got to be I I I imagine it's very difficult to be in a locker room where you know that's what they're going to end up doing. It feels like everybody's kind of pleading their case to find a new s- landing spot. >> Well, and this is a team too where I think that the Jaguars stack up nicely against them, right? Because it's all predicated through Jonathan Taylor. Like whether it's in the run game or the pass game, they try to get Jonathan Taylor going. And if the Jaguars have shown one thing, probably the purest constant so far this season is the Jaguars can stop the run. >> They can. >> And and the other part of that is they might be trying to showcase him, too. >> Yeah, yeah. >> Maybe. See who can come get. >> Put him Put him in the window so everybody can see what they got. >> Don't don't don't put him in the window in Jacksonville, P. You might want to just, you know, put him in the in the back display for another week and then bring him back out for display. >> I'll round out the division with the Titans who fall to the Browns. Browns got a 27-24 win. What's that rebuild looking like, Pete? Obviously, their win record is not great. Is this Salah's going to have some time to figure it out? It's going to be a one-and-done? What do you feel the vibes are there? >> I don't think it's a one-and-done, but man, the quarterback's thrown for over 200 yards once all season, one time. And he just doesn't look right. He missed a shot in the middle of the field that would have been a touchdown on Sunday, and then he came back and he made a play and they scored to tie the game, but then you let them go right down the field and win it. And and so they're it's just not a very good football team right now. But I don't know how you hire Salah when you know the talent level isn't great and give him only 1 year. >> Uh so I think I think he's okay, but if you know, they're just not doing anything really Tony Pollard had a good game on Sunday. He ran the ball well, but they don't throw it well enough. And and I think that's the biggest problem. There's a lot of questions about uh the quarterback. And if he doesn't get it going, I think that's going to be a problem for them. >> Yeah, it seemed like last year, you know, the conversation was, well, he doesn't have any weapons, right? So he's got nothing to throw to. And and and this year, you know, they addressed it in the draft a little bit. They addressed it in other areas. And now the conversation seems to be okay, is he the guy or not, right? And and any time you start having those questions of, you know, is your quarterback, is he a franchise guy? Well, you don't really have a good team. So until they figure that out, whether Cam Ward's going to be their franchise guy or not, they're they're going to be bottom of the of the pack. >> It's always hard when you come in and you get a new coaching regime in there cuz he's not their guy.
